policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Ketiv בצחחיים and qere בַּצְּחִיחִים are spellings of the same noun (bare/open places); ASV 'in the open places' renders either identically, has no italic supply and no textual note on the unit, so the English cannot distinguish them. Base (qere) fallback retained.

Ketiv ונשוב (plene) and qere וַנָּשָׁב are orthographic forms of the same wayyiqtol 'and we returned'; ASV 'that we returned' renders either identically, with no italic supply and no textual note mapped to the unit. Base (qere) fallback retained.
